To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a CZE method was developed for quantitative analysis of Cyasorb 3529 in polymer materials, based on a detailed characterization of the oligomer structure of this HALS by CZE‐Q‐TOF‐MS. Quant
a comprehensive characterization of Cyasorb3529 by CZE‐Q‐TOF‐MS was performed, allowing the identification of 32 oligomers and the development of a quantitative method based on CZE‐UV detection.
a CZE method using UV detection and hexamethyl melamine as internal standard can be used for the quantitation, based on the triazine ring of Cyasorb3529 in real samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantitative assessment of Cyasorb3529 in polymer matrices.

the development of a novel CZE‐QMS method for the quantitative analysis of Cyasorb‐3529 in real polymer materials, which allows the determination of oligomer composition and concentration of this HALS.
the quantitative analysis of HALS by means of CZE and QTOF MS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CZE method developed with UV detection and QTOF MS detection allows the identification of all oligomer peaks of the Cyasorb 3329 standard, and the quantitative determination of all oligomers of this HALS present in real polymer samples.
the combination of CZE with UV‐ and QTOF-MS detection allows the quantitative analysis of Cyasorb® 3529 in polymer samples, even if the oligomer composition is not known a priori.
the CZE method with UV detection and the QTOF‐mass spectrometer detection can be used as a complementary tool to quantify Cyasorb 2529 oligomers in a real polymer sample.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of UV and QTOF MS detection in CZE is a powerful tool for the identification and quantitation of HALS in polymer samples.
CZE‐Q‐TOF‐MS can be successfully applied to characterize and quantify HALSs in polymer samples, even in cases where the oligomer composition is changing during processing.
CZE‐Q‐TOF‐MS can be successfully used for the characterization of oligomeric HALS and the subsequent quantitative analysis of HALS in real samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CZE‐Q‐TOF‐MS can be used as a tool for in‐depth investigations on the oligomeric composition of HALS and other stabilizers in polymers.
the use of a UV detector in combination with CZE‐MS/MS can be a powerful tool for the analysis of complex mixtures.
the correct quantitation of a HALS in a polymer material can only be achieved if the oligomeric composition of this HALST is known and if the oligomers can be quantitated separately.
